VBO:0200216.summary: Reliability and a cooperative manner are central to the Bracco Italiano's working character. Its standard describes a docile, responsive pointing dog shaped by Italy's bird-hunting traditions, with retrieval among its established skills. The chestnut-roan variety belongs to the same Italian pointing breed, selected for a fast, ground-covering trot in the field.
VBO:0200216.shortDescription: A reliable, cooperative Italian pointing dog, with bird-finding and retrieving woven into its working history.

sources.title: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Standard 202: Bracco Italiano
sources.evidence: FCI202 Behavior/Temperament directly describes reliable, docile, understanding and trainable hunting character; calibrated cooperative/responsive paraphrases. Utilization is pointing; Historical Summary describes Italian bird hunting, retrieval and selection for fast wide trot. Coat names white speckled brown/liver roan, distinct from orange roan or plain white with brown patches. Tail natural not belowhock; short dense coat, long rounded drop ears and characteristic head support morphology. No measured age/size, child suitability, guaranteed training result or color-specific behavior used.

VBO:0200469.summary: Friendly and calm, the Markiesje tends to combine a companion’s watchfulness with an active, sociable character. Also called the Dutch Tulip Hound, it is known for joining its people on outings. Enthusiasts began rebuilding the breed in the 1970s, and Dutch national recognition followed in 1999.
VBO:0200469.shortDescription: An alert, friendly Dutch companion with a calm manner, an active side and a fondness for joining its people on outings.

sources.title: Nederlandse Markiesjes Vereniging — breed history and complete standard
sources.evidence: Own history places revival in the mid-1970s and Dutch national recognition in 1999. Standard describes friendly, calm, intelligent character and an active sociable companion. Morphology guidance only: slightly longer-than-tall light build, silky black coat with feathering, drop ears, hock-length natural tail carried merrily or downcurved and never curled over the back. Claims do not imply FCI recognition, pedigree registration of the photo subject, individual suitability or health promises.

sources.title: Raad van Beheer — Markiesje breed page
sources.evidence: Character section calls the dog watchful and friendly and says it likes going everywhere with its owner; supports the companionship/outings sentence as a tendency. Text is supplied by breed clubs, not substantively reviewed by the host. FCI status is explicitly not recognized; omitted from prose apart from correctly limited Dutch national recognition.

sources.title: Markiesje Society of America — history and English alternate name
sources.evidence: Actual history explicitly calls Markiesjes 'also known as Dutch Tulip Hounds'; supports exact alternate-name mapping to catalog0469. Medieval/aristocratic continuity, kings, naming legends and numerical population assertions are excluded.

VBO:0201055.summary: Multi-colored Poodles often seek close company and bring a playful streak to shared activities. Their social nature helps explain the breed's long involvement in performance events, while larger Poodles retain the background of hunting companions. Patterned and solid-colored Poodles are shown separately in UKC conformation, but are the same breed.
VBO:0201055.shortDescription: Multi-colored Poodles tend to seek close company, with a playful streak and a long tradition of shared activities.

sources.title: UKC Multi-Colored Poodle official breed standard (revised January 1, 2025)
sources.evidence: Characteristics: highly social, close human companionship, sense of humor and performance activities. History scopes Miniature/Toy to companions. Explicit note: solid and multi-colored are separate conformation exhibits, not separate breeds. Color section establishes abstract/parti/phantom/sable/brindle patterns.

sources.title: UKC Multi-Colored Standard Poodle official breed standard (revised January 2, 2024)
sources.evidence: Characteristics: highly social, close human companionship, sense of humor and performance activities; history explicitly gives Standard Poodles hunting-companion background. Note states solid/multi-colored not separate breeds. Tail and natural-tail policy support complete natural tail; patterns include abstract and parti.

VBO:0200611.summary: Friendliness, confidence and close companionship are central aims of Goldendoodle breeding. GANA's standard emphasizes a steady temperament for this Golden Retriever–Poodle cross. Its open stud book includes crosses from the two founding breeds and later-generation Goldendoodles, so the type covers a range of sizes and coats.
VBO:0200611.shortDescription: Bred for friendly, confident companionship, this Golden Retriever–Poodle cross comes in varied sizes and coats.

sources.title: Goldendoodle Association of North America — Goldendoodle Breed Standard
sources.evidence: General Appearance explicitly specifies friendly/confident companion function, Poodle and Golden Retriever as the only founding breeds, open stud book with founding-breed or multigenerational crosses, and diversity of sizes/coats. Temperament specifies friendly/reliable temperament as selection criteria. These are attributed breeding aims; summary/short omit hypoallergenic, health, service/therapy suitability promises and universal behavior.

VBO:0200308.summary: An energetic, reliable example is Tasha, a Cavajack whose club recorded seven years of flyball racing and a Flyball Master Champion title. Flyball pairs hurdle running with ball retrieval in a relay. Also called Jackalier, the Cavajack is a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel–Jack Russell Terrier cross.
VBO:0200308.shortDescription: Cavajack Tasha raced in flyball for seven years; this cross is also called Jackalier.

sources.title: Australian Flyball Association — 2026 Hawkesbury Show flyball catalogue, Tasha retirement tribute
sources.evidence: Entire ten-page extracted text personally read, and whole native page9 render read. Norwest Thunderdogs page9 calls named Tasha a reliable little Cavajack and energetic club member, records seven years racing and Flyball Master Champion title. Final full and short describe Tasha alone. No population temperament, parent inheritance, family suitability or claim the portrait depicts Tasha. Adjacent Twix tribute excluded.

sources.title: Australian Flyball Association — What is Flyball?
sources.evidence: Entire2158B extracted current home body read. Official sport definition has two relay teams of four dogs, four hurdles, box-triggered ball retrieval and return. Profile paraphrases hurdle running and ball retrieval in a relay; no general Cavajack ability or suitability claim.

sources.title: Terrier Owner — Josh Martin, Cav-A-Jack definition and breed names
sources.evidence: Entire15858B actual extracted page including byline/body/nav/footer personally read. Introduction defines Cav-A-Jack as Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and Jack Russell Terrier cross; Breed Names table includes Cavajack and Jackalier. Used only for lexical cross definition and alias. Josh Martin is site founder and JRT owner; not claimed firsthand Cavajack experience or veterinary expertise. All parent-temperament extrapolation, Luna anecdotes, health/training/suitability/guarantee claims excluded.
